U.S. stock futures were indecisive ahead of the October jobs data, which may shape expectations for interest rates and broader demand for the market.

Also on investors' radar screens were Advanced Micro Devices and SanDisk after recent setbacks in the semiconductor industry.

The sale has prompted issues about valuations and the speed of investing on A.I. infrastructure. But profits reflected a different story for certain technology-related enterprises.

Cloudflare topped quarterly revenue estimates and lifted its yearly prediction, while Airbnb posted increased bookings and a stronger outlook.

Those results underscored ongoing demand for cloud services and travel, even amid broader market turmoil.

For semiconductor investors, the immediate question is whether the drops Thursday were a momentary correction of valuations or a reflection of deeper worries about the outlook for growth.

The next trigger is the October U.S. employment report and how the market interprets it for interest rates and technology spending.

title: Qualcomm Rises 5% on Alphabet’s $548 Million Stake as CEO Sees a “Disconnect” on AI

Qualcomm Rises 5% on Alphabet's $548 Million Stake as CEO Sees a "Disconnect" on AI ©@undefined from Getty Images Pro via Canva, @Stefan Dinse from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Qualcomm shares rose 5% today on Alphabet's nearly $548 million stake.

The stake backs Qualcomm's data center push, still targeting $5 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027.

Arm and Intel have a lot riding on that push too.

Qualcomm trades above its five-year average forward P/E as earnings shrink, so data center revenue has to show up.

Qualcomm (QCOM:NASDAQ) jumped 5% today after Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ) disclosed a stake of nearly $548 million, a vote for its push into data centers. That's a day after it sank 12% on a 26% drop in handset chip revenue.

Two chipmakers have a lot riding on that push: Arm Holdings (ARM:NASDAQ), which licenses the designs Qualcomm's CPUs run on, and Intel (INTC:NASDAQ), whose server chips Qualcomm wants to compete with.

A second hyperscaler buys in

Alphabet's 13F shows roughly 3 million Qualcomm shares at the end of September.

On Wednesday, CEO Cristiano Amon kept the $5 billion fiscal 2027 data center target, mostly from two hyperscalers, one of them Amazon. Amazon already holds a warrant for up to 25 million Qualcomm shares. Now another cloud giant owns the stock.

Short on everything

Asked by Yahoo Finance today about the AI sell-off, Amon pointed to an industry "short on wafers." He thinks "there may be a disconnect in what the market probably expects the rates of build out and the actual rate of build out."

Intel, up 7% today, has the same problem. Its data center and AI revenue jumped 78% in the September quarter, and CEO Lip-Bu Tan's priority is unlocking supply "to meet extraordinary demand for our Xeon family." That's an opening for Qualcomm.

If Qualcomm wins that business, Arm, up 3%, gets a cut. Its data center royalties more than doubled year over year in each of the four quarters through June. But phones were still about 43% of its royalties in the year to March 2026, so Qualcomm's handset slump hurts Arm, too.

The numbers still have to catch up

Going into Wednesday's report, analysts expected Qualcomm's earnings to dip again in fiscal 2027:

Qualcomm (QCOM): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (years to September) (TIKR)

And the stock isn't cheap against its own history:

Qualcomm (QCOM): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

At the last close, it traded at about 18x forward earnings, above its five-year average of 14x, and today's jump takes it higher.

Alphabet's vote is welcome. But at that multiple, with earnings shrinking, I'd want to see data center revenue before buying this bounce.

AMD Soars 10%, Intel Up 7% as Chip Stocks Rebound From Election Sell-Off ©@undefined from Getty Images Pro via Canva, @Kittipong Jirasukhanont from PhonlamaiPhoto's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

AMD shares are up 10% today after a 17% plunge on fears Democrats' midterm wins will slow the data center buildout.

AMD posted record revenue of $13.4 billion on Tuesday and guided to about $17 billion for the fourth quarter.

Intel, Broadcom and Arista Networks are rebounding too.

The main risk: AMD's 2027 earnings, which analysts expect to more than double, depend on data centers getting built on time.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) stock is up 10% today. That wins back part of Thursday's 17% plunge.

Intel (INTC:NASDAQ), Broadcom (AVGO:NASDAQ) and Arista Networks (ANET:NYSE) are bouncing back too.

Democrats' midterm sweep set off the rout because investors feared tighter rules for AI data centers. But Gavekal's U.S. chief economist Will Denyer said even if newly elected governors make building harder, "There will always be some state and some county who is willing to welcome data centers."

AMD just had a record quarter

AMD's Data Center sales rose 97% to $8.5 billion last quarter, and total revenue hit a record $13.4 billion.

Analysts expect AMD's normalized EPS to more than double in 2027:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

AMD's fourth-quarter guide came in above analysts' own forecasts, so they have more reason to raise those numbers than to cut them.

The buildout hasn't slowed yet

Intel, up 7%, says the demand is still there. Its data center sales jumped 78% to $7.3 billion last quarter. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said its "immediate priority is to unlock additional supply to meet extraordinary demand for our Xeon family."

So do the companies that build those data centers. Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ), up 6%, now expects $72 billion to $82 billion of sales in its fiscal year ending June 2027. Arista, up [X%], grew third-quarter revenue 58.5%, its fastest since its IPO.

TIKR tracks 53 analysts on AMD. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AMD, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AMD's Analyst Ratings

AMD isn't priced for delays

AMD has said its 2027 outlook depends on customers bringing data centers online in time. New rules could slow exactly that.

Yet AMD trades at 42x forward earnings. That's above its five-year average of 35x but below its 67x June peak:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

At today's price, it's even higher.

Broadcom, up 2%, is the cheaper way into the same AI budgets at 19x. But analysts expect its EPS to grow 67% in its fiscal 2027, against AMD's 110%. Investors pay up for that gap.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) is drawing fresh attention after a sharp decline. The stock fell 10.2% on Thursday and 26.31% over the past month as a Nasdaq sell-off battered Asian chip stocks. The drop came even as the company's fundamentals kept strengthening.

24/7 Wall St.

My thesis is simple: the world's AI hardware runs through TSMC's fabs. On the October earnings call, C.C. Wei said it himself: "All the AI players are working with TSMC."

Why Election Week Strengthened My Position

Americans just voted, and the policy that matters most to my holding is already written into the tax code. Section 48D grants a credit equal to 35% of qualified investment in U.S. advanced manufacturing facilities (26 U.S.C. § 48D(a)), and it covers projects that begin construction by December 31, 2026. Federal subsidies help fund TSMC's U.S. expansion and take some geographic pressure off the company. Construction of the second Arizona fab is complete, and volume production should begin in the third quarter of 2027. TSMC has also sent teams to evaluate Texas. Lawmakers are buying too: three House members reported TSM purchases this year, the latest dated September 22, 2026.

Three Numbers That Keep Pulling Me Back

Growth keeps accelerating. Third-quarter revenue reached $46.72 billion, up 41.2% in dollar terms. Over the year, management lifted its 2026 outlook from close to 30% growth to approximately 44%.

Pattern Behind the Pain

Semis dominate. Chip designers and equipment makers (Marvell, Lam, Teradyne, Arm) took the heaviest hits. They are the most direct way to bet on data-center capex.

Memory and storage got hit hardest. SanDisk fell 22.3% in a day, Seagate 16.2% and Kioxia 20.8%.

NVIDIA looks mild by comparison. It fell 9.3% on the day, its worst since January 2025, and its RSI is still in the oversold zone.

Bounce or Trap?

Bull case: Premarket Friday already showed a rebound. Lam Research was up about 13%, Marvell about 10%, and SanDisk about 10.6% (Nov 6, 2026). Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 1.4%. Oversold readings often precede relief rallies.

Bear case: An oversold reading doesn't mean the selling is over. A Nov 6 analysis warned that more pain may come for AI infrastructure names as investors reassess demand after the election. The 10-year yield is near 4.87% after a strong jobs report, which pressures high-multiple growth stocks. The Nasdaq is also in correction territory and headed for a fourth straight weekly decline.
